mainTopic: 'בבגדו בה' and the argument over יש אם למקרא and יש אם למסורת; רבה בר אבוה's question whether יעוד makes נישואין or אירוסין, and the attempts to prove it from two ברייתות
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about the words 'בבגדו בה' in the פסוק about a Jewish maidservant (אמה העבריה). רבי עקיבא reads them as 'his garment': once the master marries her, her father can no longer sell her. רבי אליעזר reads them as 'betrayal': a father who sold her once cannot sell her again. The גמרא explains that they argue over whether we learn from how a word is read aloud (מקרא) or how it is spelled (מסורת), and that רבי שמעון learns from both. Next, רבה בר אבוה asks whether יעוד makes the maidservant fully married (נישואין) or only betrothed (אירוסין). The גמרא first tries to prove 'אירוסין' from the garment ברייתא, but רב נחמן בר יצחק says that ברייתא is about ordinary betrothal. A second proof comes from a ברייתא that lets a father sell his widowed daughter to a כהן גדול, which רבי יצחק explains as a girl widowed from יעוד. The גמרא then shows that the same difficulty exists if יעוד is only אירוסין, so the proof seems to fall. The amud ends as the גמרא starts to argue that betrothal and marriage cannot be compared, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: once the master spreads his garment over her, the father cannot sell her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי עקיבא's reading of 'בבגדו בה': once the master has spread his garment over the maidservant, which means he has taken her as a wife, her father can no longer sell her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he has spread his garment over her, the father may no longer sell her. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא explaining the פסוק about an אמה העבריה. רבי עקיבא explains 'בבגדו בה' as 'with his garment upon her'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading a garment over a woman is a sign of taking her as a wife, and here it means the master's יעוד. For רבי עקיבא, the פסוק teaches that after she is married to the master, her father can never again sell her as a maidservant.

keyTerms.meaning: He spread his garment over her, a sign of taking her as a wife
Allowed, permitted
A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant
The master's designation of the maidservant as his wife

phrases.english: Once he has spread his garment over her,
phrases.notes: This explains the words 'בבגדו בה' in שמות 21:8, which the ברייתא quoted just before this point.

phrases.english: he may no longer sell her,
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the girl's father.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, once the master marries the maidservant (spreads his garment over her), her father can no longer sell her.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: once the father has betrayed her, he cannot sell her again
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'בבגדו בה' as coming from the word for betrayal: once the father betrayed his daughter by selling her one time, he may not sell her again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'בבגדו בה' means that once he has betrayed her, he may no longer sell her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a different reading of the same words. He reads 'בבגדו' as 'his betrayal' and not 'his garment'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר the 'betrayal' is the father's first sale of his daughter. Because of that, the פסוק teaches that a father cannot sell his daughter as a maidservant a second time. So the two תנאים draw two different laws from the same word.

keyTerms.meaning: The words from שמות 21:8, read as 'his garment' or as 'his betrayal'
Betrayed, dealt unfaithfully

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"When he betrays her" (בבגדו בה) —
once he has betrayed her,
phrases.notes: The father 'betrayed' her when he sold her the first time.

phrases.english: he may no longer sell her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different reading of the same words that רבי עקיבא explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a father who sold his daughter once may not sell her again.

steps.title: What are they really arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic principle stands behind the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It wants to find the deeper principle that makes these two תנאים read the same word in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both read the same פסוק, but each comes out with a different meaning. The גמרא assumes there must be a general rule of how to read the Torah that they disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the argument presented in steps 1 and 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which general principle of reading the Torah divides רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Spelling versus pronunciation: יש אם למסורת and יש אם למקרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from how the word is spelled (מסורת), which points to 'betrayal'. רבי עקיבא learns from how it is read aloud (מקרא), which points to 'garment'. רבי שמעון learns from both, so he holds both laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds that the spelling is the main source. רבי עקיבא holds that the pronunciation is the main source. רבי שמעון holds that both the pronunciation and the spelling count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about whether we learn laws from the way a word is written in the Torah or from the way it is traditionally read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written letters of 'בבגדו' can be read as 'betrayal', so רבי אליעזר, who follows the spelling, learns that the father cannot sell her twice. The traditional reading is 'his garment', so רבי עקיבא, who follows the pronunciation, learns that she cannot be sold after marriage. רבי שמעון uses both readings, so he holds both laws: no sale after marriage, and no second sale.

keyTerms.meaning: The spelling of the Torah is the main source for learning laws
The traditional reading (pronunciation) of the Torah is the main source for learning laws
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two terms. מסורת is the written spelling, the letters on the page. מקרא is how the word is read out loud with its vowels.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר follows the spelling (betrayal, so no second sale). רבי עקיבא follows the reading (garment, so no sale after marriage). רבי שמעון follows both, so he holds both laws.
steps.whyThisMatters: The argument over יש אם למקרא and יש אם למסורת comes up in many places in ש״ס, so it is worth knowing these two terms well.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds: the written spelling is the main source,
phrases.notes: Literally 'there is a mother to the tradition.' He means the way the word is written is what we learn from.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva holds: the reading is the main source,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא וְלַמָּסוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon holds: both the reading and the spelling are sources.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר learns from the spelling, רבי עקיבא from the pronunciation, and רבי שמעון from both.

steps.title: רבה בר אבוה asks: does יעוד count as full marriage or only betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה asks whether the master's יעוד of the maidservant makes her fully married (נישואין) or only betrothed (אירוסין). He lists three practical differences: inheriting her, becoming טמא for her as a כהן, and annulling her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה asked: Does יעוד create full marriage, or does it create only betrothal? The practical difference is whether he inherits her, whether he becomes ritually impure for her, and whether he can annul her vows. What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Once the master designates the maidservant as his wife, what stage of marriage is she in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband inherits his wife, a כהן may become טמא to bury his wife, and a husband annuls his wife's vows by himself, but all of this applies only after full נישואין. During אירוסין he does not inherit her or become טמא for her, and he annuls her vows only together with her father. So the answer decides all three laws.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, he raised a question (often one with no clear answer)
Full marriage
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
The practical difference that comes out of the question
Annulling vows

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh asked:
Does designation create full marriage,
or does it create only betrothal?
The practical difference is whether he inherits her,
and whether he becomes impure for her, and whether he annuls her vows. What is the answer?
phrases.notes: 'Becomes impure for her' means a כהן, who may become טמא to bury his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about יעוד, the act described in רבי עקיבא's reading
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יעוד creates נישואין or only אירוסין

steps.title: Come and hear: the ברייתא about the garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא again (רבי עקיבא's reading) as a possible source to answer רבה בר אבוה's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'בבגדו בה' means that once he has spread his garment over her, the father may no longer sell her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question. In this step it only quotes the ברייתא; the proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ברייתא from step 1 is now used for a new purpose. The goal is to look carefully at its exact wording, 'he may not sell her', and draw a conclusion about יעוד.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"With his garment upon her" (בבגדו בה) —
once he has spread his garment over her
he may no longer sell her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to answer the question of step 5
steps.raayaObject: Whether יעוד creates נישואין or אירוסין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי עקיבא on 'בבגדו בה'

steps.title: Reading closely: he cannot sell her, but he can still designate her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. It only says the father cannot sell her, which implies he can still designate her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Selling her is what he cannot do. But designating her, that he can still do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from what the ברייתא says and from what it leaves out. It forbids only selling, so the father must still have some power over her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father had no power over her at all, the ברייתא would not limit itself to selling. Since it mentions only selling, the father still keeps the right to designate her for marriage. This inference sets up the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To sell
He can still designate her

phrases.english: Selling her is what he cannot do,
but designating her, that he can still do,
phrases.notes: The father can still designate her for marriage to someone else, for example if the master dies or divorces her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That the father still has power over her after יעוד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא forbids only selling, not designating

steps.title: If יעוד were full marriage the father would have no power left, so it must be betrothal
steps.stepSummary: If יעוד created full נישואין, the father would lose all power over her. Since he can still designate her, יעוד must create only אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that יעוד creates full marriage, then once she is married her father has no more authority over her! So must we not learn from here that it creates only betrothal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the inference from step 7 only works if יעוד is אירוסין, and it suggests that this answers רבה בר אבוה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After full נישואין a father loses all authority over his daughter. During אירוסין he still keeps some rights. Since the ברייתא implies the father keeps the right to designate her, she must be only betrothed, so יעוד makes אירוסין. The words 'אלא לאו' show this is offered as a proof, and the גמרא may still test it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say
Authority, power
Rather, must we not learn from here?

steps.confusionAlert: This is a suggested proof ('אלא לאו'), not yet a final ruling. Wait to see whether the גמרא accepts it or pushes it away.

phrases.english: And if you say that it creates full marriage,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּנִישֵּׂאת שׁוּב אֵין לְאָבִיהָ רְשׁוּת בָּהּ!
phrases.english: once she is married her father no longer has any authority over her!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵירוּסִין עוֹשֶׂה.
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that it creates only betrothal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference of step 7 to answer the question of step 5
steps.raayaSupportSource: The father still keeps the right to designate her (step 7), which is impossible after full נישואין
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Suggested answer: יעוד creates אירוסין, not נישואין.

steps.title: The earlier proof is rejected: the ברייתא is about ordinary betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתא is not talking about יעוד at all. It means that once a father betroths his daughter in a normal way, he can no longer sell her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here the ברייתא is dealing with ordinary betrothal. This is what it means: once her father has handed her over to a man who is obligated to give her food, clothing, and marital relations, he can no longer sell her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from steps 7-8. It reads the ברייתא as talking about a normal husband, not a master who did יעוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof depended on reading the ברייתא as being about יעוד. If the ברייתא is really about ordinary קידושין, it tells us nothing about whether יעוד makes אירוסין or נישואין. So רבה בר אבוה's question is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary betrothal, the normal kind, not through יעוד
Food, clothing, and marital relations: the three things a husband owes his wife
"And this is what it means": the גמרא is reading the text in a new way

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Here it is dealing with ordinary betrothal.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא from steps 6-8, the one that says the father cannot sell her.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
Once her father handed her over
to one who became obligated in her food, her clothing, and her marital relations,
he can no longer sell her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּקִידּוּשִׁין דְּעָלְמָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 7-8 by putting the ברייתא in a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא about the father not being able to sell her.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was about יעוד. It can be read as being about ordinary קידושין instead.

steps.title: A new source: selling a daughter to relatives or to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. The תנא קמא says a father cannot sell his daughter to relatives. רבי אליעזר says he can. Both agree he can sell her as a widow to a כהן גדול, or as a divorcee or חלוצה to a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: He may not sell her to relatives. In the name of רבי אליעזר they said: He may sell her to relatives. And they agree that he may sell her as a widow to a כהן גדול, and as a divorcee or a חלוצה to a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer רבה בר אבוה's question by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source. The proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives she is forbidden to marry can never do יעוד with her, so the תנא קמא says she cannot be sold to them. A widow married to a כהן גדול is forbidden, but קידושין still takes effect, so יעוד is possible and both sides agree the sale works. The key detail for the proof is the word "widow".

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives, here meaning ones she is forbidden to marry
"And they agree": a point both sides accept
A widow released from יבום through חליצה. She is forbidden to a כהן
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Come and hear:
He may not sell her to relatives.
In the name of Rabbi Eliezer they said:
He may sell her to relatives.
And they agree that he may sell her as a widow to a High Priest,
and as a divorcee or a ḥalutza to a common priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a new ברייתא to answer the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether יעוד makes נישואין or only אירוסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about selling a daughter to relatives and to כהנים, including selling her as a widow.

steps.title: What kind of widow can her father still sell?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this widow became a widow. If she betrothed herself as a minor, that betrothal does not count, so she would not be called a widow. If her father betrothed her, then he should no longer be able to sell her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this widow? If you say she betrothed herself, would she be called a widow? But if her father betrothed her, can he sell her? A person cannot sell his daughter as a maidservant after she has been married!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is working out exactly what kind of widow the ברייתא means. Both simple cases fail, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's betrothal of herself does not work, so she is not truly a widow. A betrothal by her father does work, but then the rule is that a father cannot sell her after אישות. So the ברייתא needs some other kind of widowhood.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the case?": asks for the exact situation
"If you say": tests one possible answer
"Rather": moves on to the other possibility
Being married or betrothed to a man

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that the daughter here is a minor. That is why betrothing herself has no effect, and why her father holds the power to betroth or sell her.

phrases.english: This widow, what is the case?
If you say she betrothed herself,
would one call her a widow?
phrases.notes: A minor's own betrothal doesn't take effect, so she was never really his wife.

phrases.english: Rather, her father betrothed her.
Can he then sell her?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: But a person may not sell his daughter
into servitude after marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the word "widow" in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly how the widow in the ברייתא became a widow, given that her father can still sell her.

steps.title: She was widowed from יעוד, following רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם, quoting רבי יצחק, says the case is a girl widowed from קידושי יעוד. This follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who holds that the original sale money was not given for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב עמרם said in the name of רבי יצחק: Here it is talking about betrothal through יעוד, and it follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, who said: The first money was not given for betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 11. The widow was sold as a maidservant, the master did יעוד, and then he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third way to become a widow, different from the two cases that failed in step 11. The ruling follows רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's view that the sale money was not betrothal money. Steps 14-15 show why that view matters here.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal created when the master designates the maidservant as a wife
"According to the view of"
The first money, the money paid when she was sold as a maidservant

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: And Rav Amram said that Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
Here it is dealing with betrothal of designation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
The first money was not given for betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּקִדּוּשֵׁי יִעוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by finding a kind of widowhood that fits the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the ברייתא in a specific case (widowed from יעוד) and follows one specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only possible widows were one who betrothed herself, which doesn't count, or one betrothed by her father, who could not be sold again.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was widowed from קידושי יעוד, according to רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.

steps.title: So יעוד cannot create full נישואין
steps.stepSummary: If יעוד made her fully married, her father would have lost all power over her. Yet the ברייתא lets him sell her again. So יעוד must create only אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say יעוד creates full marriage: once she has been married, her father no longer has any authority over her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The father can sell this widow again, which would be impossible if יעוד had created full נישואין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a daughter is fully married (נישואין), her father loses all authority over her for good. The ברייתא says the father can sell this widow-from-יעוד to a כהן גדול, so he still has authority. That means יעוד only made אירוסין.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you say": tests the opposite side to show it can't work
Authority, power over someone

steps.whatToRemember: Suggested proof from the widow sold to a כהן גדול: the father can sell her after she was widowed from יעוד, which seems to show that יעוד makes only אירוסין. The next steps challenge this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof stood, it would answer רבה בר אבוה's question: whether the master inherits her, becomes טמא for her, and can annul her vows. All three belong to full נישואין, not to אירוסין. The next steps test whether the proof holds.

phrases.english: And if you say it creates full marriage,
once she has been married
her father no longer has authority over her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case set up in step 12 to finish the proof for רבה בר אבוה's question.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing a father to sell his daughter as a widow (widowed from יעוד) to a כהן גדול.

steps.title: Even betrothal should block a second sale
steps.stepSummary: If יעוד creates only אירוסין, the ברייתא is still hard to understand, because a father cannot sell his daughter after אירוסין either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then, are you saying יעוד creates only אירוסין? Then how can the ברייתא say they agree he may sell her? A man cannot sell his daughter as a maidservant after she has been married, and that includes betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 13. It shows that saying 'only אירוסין' does not solve the problem either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said: full נישואין would end the father's power, so יעוד must be only אירוסין. But in step 11 the rule 'no sale after אישות' already blocked selling a widow whose father had betrothed her, so it covers אירוסין too. That means אירוסין should block the sale as well, and the ברייתא still looks hard.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
And they agree, meaning the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר
Being sold as a maidservant
Being married to a man. Here it includes betrothal.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against the ברייתא. The גמרא is showing that the proof in step 13 runs into the same problem it was trying to avoid.

phrases.english: But rather, what? It creates betrothal?
phrases.notes: 'It' means יעוד, the master designating the maidservant as his wife.

phrases.english: And they agree that he may sell her?!
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 10.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: But a person does not sell his daughter
into servitude after matrimony!
phrases.notes: This is the same rule quoted in step 11. There it already blocked selling a widow whose father had betrothed her, so it covers betrothal too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof just given in step 13 by showing that its own conclusion faces the same difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 13 that יעוד creates only אירוסין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father cannot sell his daughter after אישות, which includes אירוסין (the rule quoted in step 11). So the ברייתא's permission to resell her is just as hard if יעוד creates only אירוסין.

steps.title: The same answer works for full marriage too
steps.stepSummary: Whatever answer saves the 'only אירוסין' view also saves the 'full נישואין' view, so the proof falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you have to answer? That her own אירוסין is different from אירוסין done by her father. But then, even if you say יעוד creates נישואין, you can say her own נישואין is different from נישואין done by her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the only possible answer for the 'אירוסין' view works equally well for the 'נישואין' view. So the ברייתא proves nothing either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To defend the 'אירוסין' view, you must say the rule against reselling applies only when the father himself arranged the betrothal, not when it came through יעוד. That same split can be made for נישואין. So the ברייתא cannot decide between the two views, and the proof from step 13 is knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage, the second stage
Her own, here meaning the marriage that came through יעוד
Is different
Even if you say

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
Her own betrothal is different
phrases.notes: 'Her own' means the betrothal that came through יעוד, not through her father's act.

phrases.english: from betrothal by her father?
Even if you say it creates marriage,
her own marriage is different
from marriage by her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the attack from step 14 by showing the needed answer cancels the proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof in step 13 that יעוד creates only אירוסין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answer needed to defend the 'אירוסין' view, 'her own is different from her father's', works just as well for the 'נישואין' view. So the ברייתא cannot decide between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: if an answer saves your side, check whether it saves the other side equally. If it does, the proof proves nothing.

steps.title: Betrothal and marriage may not be comparable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the split between two kinds of אירוסין makes sense, but the same split for נישואין may not hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? It makes sense that one kind of אירוסין differs from another kind of אירוסין. But one kind of נישואין from another kind of נישואין...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject step 15's comparison. It accepts the split for אירוסין but questions it for נישואין, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 claimed the 'her own vs. her father's' split works for both אירוסין and נישואין. Here the גמרא says that is not obviously true. It agrees there is a real difference between kinds of אירוסין, and it is about to explain why נישואין is different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A way of saying a comparison does not work
Granted, this part makes sense

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of a sentence. The reason why נישואין is different comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: What is this?
phrases.notes: He means: what kind of comparison is this? It doesn't work.

phrases.english: Granted, betrothal is different from betrothal,
but marriage from marriage,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵירוּסִין מֵאֵירוּסִין שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison in step 15 and tries to bring back the proof from step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Step 15's claim that the 'her own vs. her father's' split applies equally to נישואין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A difference between two kinds of אירוסין is reasonable, but it is not clear the same difference exists between two kinds of נישואין. The full reason continues on the next amud.
